title: DecisionEntry
description: Ratified choice — the precedent record. Source file: governance/decisions.json ({"entries": [DecisionEntry]}), append-only; changed precedent uses supersedes, never edits. DECISIONS.MD is the generated view.

title.description: The ruling itself in one line, so a reader who greps the journal gets the answer without opening the entry. Real examples: "Parallel dispatch admission: a per-sprint cap declared at planning" (D-0084); "Four gates became advice, and the rulings still say fail" (D-0082). "sprint changes" names the area and withholds the ruling, which is the whole content.

decision.description: The rule as it will be applied - the shape, the defaults, and what each surface does about it - written so an implementer can act without a follow-up question. Real example: "A sprint carries parallel (integer >= 1, default 1) ... The cap may be changed only while the sprint is proposed; changing it after ratification is a re-ratification, not an edit. --hotfix implies parallel 1" (D-0084). "we will allow parallel work" is a direction, not a rule: every surface would invent its own version of it.

rationale.description: What was weighed, INCLUDING the options that were rejected and what was wrong with each - that is the part a later session needs when it is tempted to undo this. Real example: "Three shapes were put to User. A: a per-sprint cap declared at planning. B: per-worktree admission. C: the app is the gate. User ruled A ... B ties a governance rule to a git detail no journal models; C would leave a hand-driven session ungated entirely" (D-0084). "it is better this way" gives the next reader nothing to weigh against.

ratified_by.description: Who ratified it: User directly, or the delegation they granted (name it). Written by `decide new` only when --authority resolved, and by `decide ratify`. ABSENT on a proposed or rejected decision (D-S039) -- nobody ratified it. A record with no `status` predates D-S039 and always carries it.

push_hold.description: HEAD sha this decision holds the push at, so decisions-pending stops counting it and the hold expires when new work lands (T-0120/I-0065).

superseded_by.description: The decision that replaced this one, stamped onto it when that decision is written. R-U10 requires provenance to distinguish live law from dead: `supersedes` points forward and a reader who lands on the OLD decision sees nothing at all, so a dead ruling read on its own is indistinguishable from current law. Six decisions were in that state when this field was added.

status.description: The decision's standing (D-S039, SX-020). `decide new` writes ratified when --authority resolved, proposed otherwise; `decide ratify` / `decide reject` move it. ABSENT on a record written before D-S039, which every reader takes as ratified with authority unknown -- never as bad. A proposed decision binds nothing: it does not retire what it supersedes and cannot be cited as a standing delegation.

authority.description: On what basis it binds: direct | app:<session> | standing:D-XXXX, or none for a proposed decision. Absent on a legacy record (read as unknown).

authority_claimed.description: An --authority `decide new` was given that did not resolve, kept for the person who reviews the proposed decision.

recorded_by.description: Who ran `decide new` -- the recorder, which is not a ratification.

prior_ratified_by.description: The free-text ratified_by a legacy record carried before a person ratified it with an authority; kept so the original claim survives.

rejected_by.description: The person who rejected it (`decide reject`).

acknowledged_by.description: The person who saw an authority-less or proposed record and kept it as it is (`decide acknowledge`); its standing is unchanged.
